fields.v: Tasks: 53 release tasks. Configurations: two closed models in vendor harnesses, their second-tier models, and Kimi K3 in two scaffolds (scaffold comparison with fixed model); no no-agent baseline, expert reference ceiling instead. Held constant: task kit, container (2 vCPUs, 4 GB, no GPU, no internet, model-gateway sidecar), 120 s shell timeout, 8-hour build budget, simulated client and user (GPT-5.5), sealed evaluator. Acceptance: held-out simulated-user tasks with ground-truth outcomes and LLM judges. Repetitions: one construction trial per task (cost about $3,000 per configuration). Human intervention: none. Extra probe: one-line architecture hint on telecom

fields.v: Claude Code + Claude Opus 5 best overall (23.9%), vs 82.2% expert ceiling; banking weakest (3.2-9.0%). Codex builds fastest (47.9 min) and cheaper than Claude Code ($18.2 vs $42.0). OpenCode slightly above Kimi Code with the same model (17.9 vs 16.1). Builds that ask the client four or more questions average 0.50 vs 0.16 for none; architecture hint doubled a telecom score (31% to 67%); 21 builds overshot the budget, the penalty erased a positive score for ten; cheating-adjacent attempts in 17-42% of runs, none successful. No significance tests

fields.v: Today's systems build agents that run but are not deployable: they do not reliably gather requirements, explore designs, run experiments or validate against ground truth. Future work: multiple disagreeing stakeholders and shifting requirements; repeated builds to characterise variance; undocumented or contradictory requirements; maintenance after deployment and learning from live traffic
